# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 2 (LAST), forking from the champion = seed (tau2 default surface; cand_0001 was
rejected and reverted). Reader = mid-tier `aws/gpt-oss-120b`: I favored deterministic code
enforcement, a LEANER toolset, and literal example-bearing param docs.

## Scoring reality I localized first (drives every decision)
`reward_basis = ['DB','COMMUNICATE']` and per-trial `reward = DB × COMMUNICATE` (both must
be 1). COMMUNICATE passes on every trial EXCEPT 11-t0, so the score is essentially
`db_check`. `action_checks` are informational and DO NOT affect reward — so changing WHICH
tool the agent calls is safe for scoring as long as the final DB state is unchanged.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks (trials) | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Confirmed-then-only-one-write (`narrated_without_action`) | 17 (t0,t1), part of 23 | one "Yes" for a multi-part change; agent executes ONE part, narrates the rest, sim ends → DB half-applied | BEHAVIORAL | Composite atomic-write `update_reservation` + REMOVE the 3 `update_*` primitives (SKILL lever 2, doctrine-correct variant) |
| 2 | Unauthorized ad-hoc voucher | 37 (t1) | `send_certificate($116)` to "convert" a non-cancellable reservation → extra write, DB≠gold (37-t0 passes WITHOUT it) | RULE/DECISION | In-body constraint on `send_certificate` |
| — | Wrong flight / grounding | 8 (t0,t1) | user asked for "same flight I took on May 10"; agent searched fresh and booked a different flight | REASONING | SKIPPED — no tool guard forces grounding on history; a loop READ tool was tried (cand_0001) and didn't help |
| — | Over-refusal (transfer vs cancel) | 19 (t0) | agent transferred instead of cancelling an eligible reservation (t1 cancels → passes) | DECISION | SKIPPED — cancel eligibility depends on cancellation REASON (not a tool arg); guard would be UNBOUNDED and flip passing 19-t1/37-t0 |
| — | Refund number miscommunicated | 11 (t0) | DB correct both trials; t0 said $1444 vs gold $5244 | COMMUNICATE/arith | SKIPPED — enriching return shape flagged risky (field-notes §2/§4) |
| — | Cancel + 3 bookings stall | 23 (t0,t1) | cancelled then never issued the 3 books | BEHAVIORAL | Not cracked — composite doesn't cover the book path |
| — | Infra `###STOP###` | 22 | user-simulator artifact | — | excluded from scoring |

## Changes made this iteration (real CODE across two tools; net toolset 14 → 12)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | in-body constraint (CODE) | `tools.py::send_certificate` | Raise unless `amount` is a positive multiple of 50 — policy compensation is $100×pax or $50×pax, always a multiple of 50; blocks the $116 voucher and any out-of-policy amount. | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only on non-multiple-of-50; only 37-t1 calls it and 37-t1 currently fails. |
| 1 | compose + remove (CODE) | `tools.py`: ADD `update_reservation`; REMOVE `update_reservation_flights/passengers/baggages` | ONE atomic call applies cabin/flights AND/OR baggages AND/OR passengers by delegating to the (still-present) primitive method bodies. Removing the primitives makes it the ONLY modify path, so confirm+execute is one call and a half-applied change is impossible. | Yes — reward ignores action names; composite is byte-identical DB to each primitive (verified). Leaner surface (12 vs 14) + "pass only what you change" doc + worked example mitigate mis-fill. |

## Verify-the-fix (ran real bodies on pristine AIRLINE_DB in venv-skillberry-tau2)
- `send_certificate`: amount 116/0/−50 → ValueError (fires); 50/100/150 → certificate added. Matches 37-t1 bad value blocked; valid policy amounts pass.
- Composite == primitive, byte-identical DB (`reservation.model_dump()` + user `payment_methods`): task 12 baggages YAX4DR (PASSING) identical; task 40 passengers 3RK2T9 identical; task 11 flights GV1N64 business→basic_economy identical (refund path); task 37 flights M20IZO economy→business identical.
- task 17 multi-part: one `update_reservation` call → cabin=economy, 1 passenger (Omar), bags 3/0, flights [HAT056,HAT138]; equals the 3 sequential primitive calls (identical DB) — the state that was half-applied before.
- Registration (adapter-filtered by REMOVE_TOOLS): exposed = 12 tools, `update_reservation` present, all 3 primitives dropped, every exposed tool yields a schema.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees: none — diagnosis via a JSON-extraction script over all 20 traces (reward_info + agent tool calls); cheaper/more reliable for arg-level facts (prior meta-insight noted subagents blow context on full trace JSONs).
- Prior iterations read: cand_0001 PROCESS + diff.patch + JOURNAL RESULT + LEDGER. Learned: keep the send_certificate guard (safe); additive composites that leave primitives exposed get routed around → this time REMOVE the primitives; drop the unused `get_reservations` helper.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- `reward = DB × COMMUNICATE`; action-name checks don't affect score → routing a modify through a composite is scoring-safe if DB is identical (proven here).
- The `send_certificate` multiple-of-50 constraint is a correct, general policy encoding — keep it.
- Do NOT re-expose the raw `update_*` primitives alongside the composite (that reproduces the stall — pitfalls doc).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- Task 8 (grounding), 19 (cancel-reason decision), 11 (COMM arithmetic), 23 (cancel+3 books): no BOUNDED tool-code lever flips DB without regression risk.
- No cancel-eligibility / basic-economy-modify / baggage-decrease / payment-count guards: none appears in a FAILING trace (not REAL), and several would be UNBOUNDED and flip passing tasks.
